doc.title: Bela Fleck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 7, 2004

title: His parents, being named Béla and his mother's music
summary: Fleck's parents split when he was young, he only recently met his father, who named the boys after classical composers. His mother played folk guitar and the family listened to the Beatles.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Do you think they had aspirations for you to be a musician?

I don’t know. I don’t think so. But my father, who — it’s a complicated story, I won’t go into too much except that I only got to meet him and get to know him over the last few years, they split up when I was really young and he named me. They had a deal, if it was

a boy he would name us, and if it was a girl, my mother would name it. It was a strange arrangement they had. And they had two boys and I got Béla, which is not a bad situation considering my brother got Ludwig.

Yeah. So my father was naming us after classical composers that he loved. So it’s a complicated story. But anyway who knows? We’re both musicians. We’re both really musical people. So it’s just bizarre. And we never heard from him.
And your mother liked what kind of music? What would she play around the house?

She played some folk guitar a little bit. Just a general open minded — not an incredibly musically oriented person although knows what she likes. We listened to a lot of Beatles when we were kids and everything that was going on in the sixties we were very into.
